geology: Low-temperature hydrothermal veins; principal antimony ore, frequently associated with gold.
intermediate: Sb2O3 (roaster/fumed oxide) or crude antimony oxide
extraction: Rich ore liquated; concentrate given a volatilizing/oxidizing roast to Sb2O3 (volatile ~900-950 C in low-O2 gas; high O2 forms non-volatile SbO2), then carbothermic reduction with soda-ash flux to regulus. Sulfur-fixation roast with ZnO/C avoids SO2.
notes: Often co-recovered with gold. Oxygen control critical to fuming.

geology: Hydrothermal veins with Pb/Cu/Sn/W deposits; bismuth is overwhelmingly a byproduct of those refining streams.
intermediate: Bi2O3 (roaster oxide) or crude bismuth bullion
extraction: Primary sulfide: roast to oxide then coke smelting/carbothermic reduction. Alkaline/molten-salt smelting with Fe2O3 sulfur-fixing agent gives ~96% Bi, co-recovering W/Mo to slag. Mostly recovered as byproduct (debismuthizing of lead, anode slimes).
notes: Supply chain dominated by Pb/Cu/W byproduct recovery rather than primary mining.

geology: Most abundant arsenic ore; high-temperature hydrothermal veins, pegmatites, contact-metamorphic settings. Common impurity in gold/copper ores.
intermediate: As2O3 (white arsenic) condensed from flue gas
extraction: Roast in air to volatilize As2O3, captured in flues/baghouse; metal made by carbothermic reduction of As2O3. Mostly recovered as byproduct from Au/Cu/Pb smelter flue dust.
notes: TOXIC. As2O3 acutely poisonous; off-gas, flue dust, and residue stabilization are key hazards. Largely a byproduct commodity.

geology: Low-temperature hydrothermal and volcanic/hot-spring deposits; arsenic sulfide minerals.
extraction: Roasting in air: 2 As2S3 + 9 O2 -> 2 As2O3 + 6 SO2; As2O3 volatilized and condensed.
notes: TOXIC. Historically used in pigments and traditional medicine; roaster gas handling is hazardous.

geology: Primary uranium oxide (UO2, grading toward U3O8); hydrothermal veins, unconformity and sandstone-hosted deposits. Pitchblende is the massive variety.
intermediate: Uranyl sulfate or uranyl tricarbonate pregnant liquor
extraction: Acid (H2SO4 -> uranyl sulfate) or alkaline (Na2CO3 -> uranyl tricarbonate) leach; purify/concentrate by ion exchange or solvent extraction; precipitate and calcine to yellowcake.
notes: RADIOACTIVE. Radon/radium and tailings are gameplay hazard hooks; yellowcake is a regulated nuclear material.

geology: Uranium silicate; common in reduced sandstone-hosted (roll-front) deposits, often intergrown with uraninite.
extraction: Leach (acid or alkaline), ion exchange / solvent extraction, precipitation, calcination to U3O8.
notes: RADIOACTIVE. Amenable to in-situ recovery (ISR) leaching.

geology: Secondary uranium-vanadium mineral in sandstone-hosted deposits (e.g., Colorado Plateau).
extraction: Salt roast then leach; separate U and V by solvent extraction / ion exchange; precipitate both.

geology: Thorium oxide in granite pegmatites and metamorphic rocks; very high Th concentration but minor commercial source.
extraction: Acid or alkaline digest/leach; solvent extraction; precipitation; calcination to ThO2.
notes: RADIOACTIVE. Not commercially mined at scale; thorium mainly a monazite byproduct.

geology: RE phosphate in mineral/beach sands; ~3-5% ThO2. Mined primarily for rare earths.
intermediate: Mixed RE/Th sulfate or hydroxide cake
extraction: Acid (conc. H2SO4) or alkaline (NaOH) digest cracks the phosphate; Th separated from REE by selective precipitation / solvent extraction via temperature and acidity control.
notes: RADIOACTIVE. CROSS-LINK: shared feed with the rare-earth catalog; Th is the radioactive co-product of REE recovery.

geology: Continental evaporite deposits near Pliocene lakes and boron-rich brines in arid basins.
extraction: Dissolution, purification, evaporation/recrystallization; acidify with H2SO4 to make boric acid.
notes: Sodium borate purified by dissolution-recrystallization; brine ops use solar evaporation ponds.

geology: Evaporite borate associated with borax beds (e.g., Kramer/Boron, California).
extraction: Dissolution, evaporation and recrystallization to borax/boric acid.
notes: Lower hydration sodium borate; processed similarly to borax.

geology: Calcium borate evaporite (major in Turkey and western USA).
extraction: Acid leach with H2SO4, then precipitation/crystallization of boric acid.
notes: Calcium borate requires acid attack rather than simple recrystallization.

geology: Hydrothermal veins and replacement deposits; gangue often galena/sphalerite/barite.
extraction: React acidspar with concentrated H2SO4 at ~250 C: CaF2 + H2SO4 -> 2 HF + CaSO4; HF purified/scrubbed. Gypsum/anhydrite byproduct.
notes: TOXIC/corrosive intermediate. Acidspar is ~60-65% of global fluorspar output and feeds all fluorochemicals. (Reduction/Refining stages here denote the acid digestion + HF purification; no metallic reduction.)

geology: Caprock of salt domes and volcanic deposits; elemental sulfur.
extraction: Frasch process melts and lifts sulfur with superheated steam and air. Burn S to SO2, then contact process to sulfuric acid.
notes: Frasch dominated supply until ~1970; now largely supplanted by recovered sulfur.

geology: Ubiquitous iron sulfide; hydrothermal, sedimentary, and massive-sulfide deposits.
extraction: Roast: 4 FeS2 + 11 O2 -> 2 Fe2O3 + 8 SO2, leaving iron-oxide cinder; SO2 fed to contact process.
notes: Historic principal sulfur source before Frasch; cinder sometimes used for iron.

geology: Hydrogen sulfide from sour natural gas and refinery streams (not a mineral; gas sweetening feed).
extraction: Claus process: partial oxidation of H2S to SO2, then 2 H2S + SO2 -> 3 S + 2 H2O; tail-gas SO2 can feed contact process.
notes: Dominant modern sulfur source. Included as a feedstock, not a mined mineral.

geology: Hydrothermal veins, bedded sedimentary, and residual deposits; barite group sulfate.
intermediate: BaS (black ash) for chemicals; direct barite for drilling mud
extraction: Most used directly as weighting agent/filler after beneficiation. For chemicals: reduction roast with coke -> BaS (black ash), then leach/precipitate to BaCO3 or BaCl2.
notes: Isostructural with celestine (complete BaSO4-SrSO4 solid solution). Bulk demand is drilling mud, used as-is.

extraction: Black-ash: reduction roast with coke at ~1100-1300 C -> SrS, then carbonation to SrCO3. Or direct conversion: react ground concentrate with Na2CO3 (+ steam) to SrCO3 + Na2SO4.
notes: SrCO3 used in glass, magnets, pyrotechnics. Complete solid solution with barite.
